utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Today in the absence of Judge Van den Wyngaert, Judge David and I sit pursuant to the provisions of Rule 15 bis. Ms. Marcus please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, VG-064. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you of the reference sheet that is in front of you with some pseudonyms of persons you may wish to refer to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Are we in open session? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yesterday before we completed, you read two paragraphs from your statement of the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: If I could ask the Court officer, please, to call up Exhibit P159, but kindly not to broadcast it. And specifically page 5 in the English, and page 4 in B/C/S. If you could scroll down slightly to the middle of the page in the English, the two paragraphs which were read begin with -- the first one is: "In the late afternoon on the same day," and the one after that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-064, when we completed yesterday, we were talking about the cars which were present during this incident, and you said, and I quote from the transcript yesterday, page 112: "I saw -- well, there was Behija Zukic's Passat in a burgundy colour, but it's not mentioned there, and that car was driven which Milan Lukic personally." I just about to ask you yesterday when we finished, how do you know whose Passat that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was Behija Zukic's Passat. Cherry red. It was the most recent type. I know this because Behija was a schoolmate of mine. We were virtually in the same street and we socialized.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You said also in this paragraph that there were some verbal threats. Could you tell us what those threats included?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Lukic made threats to us saying that we should not take on any people from other villages in our homes and that he would kill us if he saw anyone else around these parts apart from locals.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you describe how the group looked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was like this. They were wearing all sorts of clothes, some were wearing camouflage uniforms, some civilian uniforms, some had paint on their faces, different colours, black stripes on their faces like Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you describe the paint on their faces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan had black stripes across his face, applied by fingers. The others too, they had paint on their faces. Some red, some black, some blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you know Milan Lukic before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you knew Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Milan Lukic because he was a schoolmate of my husband in elementary school, so I knew him through my husband and also through Emin Vila who was Mustafa Vila's son. He disappeared in Belgrade when Belgrade was bombed and his fate is unknown. He used to work with Emin Vila in the same police station. Emin Vila was his commander. He would go to see Emin's father and I would see him there, so that's how I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who Emin Vila was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Emin Vila was Mustafa Vila's son, Jasmina's brother. Milan Lukic raped her.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, during the incident at your father-in-law's house which you read about from your statement, how far would you say you were standing from Milan Lukic as he said the things you quote him as saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a room about 12 square metres, 3 by 4. There were several of us there, so we were all huddled tightly together, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was Milan Lukic carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a rifle, and some grenades on his belt. He was armed, as was his police.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate date of this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in late May. I don't remember the exact date. I'm sorry now that I didn't write this down. There was no opportunity. It hadn't even crossed my mind to write anything down. We did our best to simply survive the affliction imposed on us by this criminal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask the court officer to please turn to page 6 in the English, which corresponds to the bottom of page 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam, can you please read to us from the bottom paragraph, the paragraph -- I'm sorry. The paragraph which begins: "One or two days later, the same group of Serbs returned." I believe it's on the bottom of page 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last paragraph begins with the words "during the night."

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I see, maybe I had the wrong corresponding page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm concerned with the nature of the questioning in this manner as tantamount to leading. I mean the problem is -- is that it's my position that the -- the Prosecution changed from viva voce to 92 ter. In the memorandum to the Trial Chamber and all of us on October 21st, this witness was indicated as a viva voce witness. Now they switched to 92 ter, of which the Court allowed that; however, the manner in which the Prosecution is tendering her statements is -- simply is allowing her to refresh her recollection before any questions are asked which, of course, is tantamount to leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, with all due respect, this witness was listed as a 92 ter witness from February in our original filing for 92 ter witnesses under the work plan she was included. The original listing of her in our 65 ter filings was also as 92 ter. In every filing which referred to this witness she was listed as 92 ter. Now, the practice that we are using with 92 ter is the identical practice that we use with all our 92 ter witnesses; that is, we seek admission of their prior statement or testimony, and then we use approximately 30 minutes to highlight certain portions and perhaps add additional detail that may not have been reflected in the statements. That's exactly what I'm doing. It will be restricted approximately to 30 minutes in total, merely highlighting. And the way that we are doing it is what the Chamber requested of us. Rather than telling her what she said in her prior statement name and asking a question, rather asking the witness to read out portions of the statement limited isolated portions, and then to ask a few follow-up -- limited follow-up questions on that particular portion of her evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think you have outlined correctly the practice which is followed here, but please try not to lead the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, Madam Witness, we were going to read from the paragraph that begins: "One or two days later, the same group of Serbs returned." Could you kindly read that for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. "One or two days later, the same group of Serbs returned. On that occasion, I heard them calling one of them Daidza. Daidza was a nickname. Daidza ordered us to bring some lamb for them to eat. The group of four women, including my cousin VG-055, Jasmina Vila, Mina Vila, and Mirsada Vila, went to fetch some lamb. As they were on their way, at a distance of about 300 metre from my house, Milan Lukic and his group stopped them. I could see them from my house. Milan Lukic ordered one of the ladies, Jasmina Vila, age 19, to take the lamb there and to go back. Daidza's group got the lamb and they went to Visegrad."

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Jasmina Vila went back to Milan Lukic as he had ordered. Milan Lukic took Jasmina to Fikreta Hodzic's place. Fikreta lived at a house where Milan Lukic stopped by. At the time, Fikreta was in her second month of pregnancy," but actually it was her third month. That's not what it says but that's what how it was. "He put them in the car and took them to Prelovo. We could see him drive off in the direction of Prelovo. "After two and a half hours, Milan Lukic brought Jasmina Vila back alone. Jasmina Vila showed us that she was black and blue with bruises all over her body. She was bleeding profusely. She was age 19 at the time. She said that Milan Lukic had raped her. Milan Lukic told her that all -- well, the locals would be tortured and killed. She also told us that Milan Lukic would be back the next day at about 10 in the morning to take her away. Jasmina's mother" --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to request a redaction of one name which was read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What line is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I am sorry. Just a moment. Just a moment, please, Your Honours. Okay. I'm sorry, it's okay. She used the pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, how do you know what you say here, that Milan Lukic ordered Jasmina Vila to return? How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that because Jasmina told us in front of my house. When she took the lamb meat away, she said, Milan Lukic had told me to go back with him. And I said, Don't go, he will take you away, he will rape you. She said, I've got to go, he will kill me unless I do. So she did. Then he put her and Fikreta in the car. I saw this happen right outside my home. He bundled them into that car and took them off to Prelog.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what vehicle he was driving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Behija's Passat, cherry red. Behija Zukic's car. He drove that car all the time. He had seized that car from Behija Zukic and killed her. She is no longer among us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you tell us exactly how Jasmina Vila looked when she returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When she returned she was all unsettled, dirty, black and blue, bleeding. I saw marks of violence and rape on her body myself. She told us the entire story, what had happened to her. He didn't take her all the way up to the house, he left her about 100 or 200 metres behind my house. She had to walk across the meadows. She was grabbing her own hair and she said, Don't allow him to kill your children. He made threats to the extent that he would chop us all to pieces, that he would kill us and burn us alive and god knows what else he mentioned. She was screaming and crying saying, Look what he has done to me. I was trying to console her but then her mother came along, took her back into the house, got her a change of clothes, washed her and took her over to a Serb's place, and the Serb's name was Novak, believing that Novak would be willing to protect her. I don't know what happened next to that girl. I'm not sure if she is alive, but somehow I don't believe that she might be.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. Your --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She also told me after he had raped her, If you're not innocent, you'll end up the same as the women over in the woods. And we had been told that there were dead bodies belonging to the women in the woods who had been mangled.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you tell us who you were referring to each time you say "he"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you explain what you mean by the words "if you are not innocent." You said: "She told me after he had raped her, If you are not innocent, you'll end up the same," et cetera. What do you mean by "innocent"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we Muslims use the word, we are talking about virginity. And a girl, for example, who has lost her virginity. Not sure how to explain that. Losing virginity, that's what it's referenced to. That she's no longer a virgin.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, you also describe in your statement a number of men being taken from your village. Did you see that incident with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you describe specifically what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were those men who were taken from my village. Milan Lukic would drive by several times. He would drive straight through the village, firing. There was this first group that he took away including Esad Zuban. We don't know where he took him. Then he came back for Rasim Sehic and his son, Enver. We learned about this from Rasim Sehic's wife. The next day she told us about this. Nevertheless, the next day I saw this for myself. There was this yellow Fico coming from the direction of Prelovo and driving on to Visegrad. In the car there was Rasim Sehic and his son.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was there any incident which you saw directly yourself in which men were taken from your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't like there was an incident. They took the men away just because they belonged to a different ethnicity, because they were Muslims, and because the objective was to cleanse Visegrad of its Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you observe the vehicles in which the men were taken?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sorry, Madam Witness. Just -- I remind you to please be careful.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I request the redaction of the witness's last answer from the public version, just the last -- the entirety of her last response.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And Madam Witness, I'm going to move on to another question now. You describe in your statement also an incident in which your husband was detained. Could you tell us, please, who detained him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Lukic's group drove up in their cars. They parked in our village. They parked along the road. Milan Lukic then searched all of the houses individually. He drove us out of our homes and herded us all into Hamed Zuban's home. So we were now all together there, including about 20 children aged 6 months to 12 years. There was a woman among the group, my husband --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and another relative of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you. I'd like to just remind you respectfully, the Chamber has admitted your statement and all the details are in there, I'd just like to ask a few particular clarifications and descriptions and that will be it for the moment. Now, may I request closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, you mentioned later in your statement that you were taken at one point to an elementary school. Can you identify for us what that elementary school was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Hasan Veletovac primary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for us what the school looked like when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't go to the school of our own free will. We were shown in, ushered in by a Serb soldier who made us go in. He jumped from the truck. He cursed at us, he drove us inside, and he said, Go in and we'll see what we do with you. And what we saw there was horrifying. When we entered the school, we saw blood on the walls and on the floor in the corridors. We found about 350 women, children, and elderly inside. There were about 150 more of us coming in. So that ultimately there were nearly 500 of us in there. I found a friend of mine inside and she told me what had happened the day before our arrival. She told us that Milan Lukic had entered the school, that he had slaughtered a man and played football with his head among the children and women and elderly who were sitting there. That he had propped the body up against the wall, the headless corpse --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: This testimony was not disclosed in any way, shape or form in the 65 ter. This was not part of her statement 2006, 1993, proofing notes or supplemental statement now of 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is this entirely new, Ms. Marcus?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honours. Your Honours, her statements include -- certainly include details, more details about the school, but actually, I'd have to check on that with regard to this particular incident, whether it was included in anything before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it part of the indictment, this incident?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No, it's not Your Honours. I can move on beyond it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would argue that none of the testimony fell within the period of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, all the testimony falls within the period of the indictment. It all relates to June of 1992. And the statements include evidence about physical abuse at the school, taking girls and women away, and even slaughtering them. The detail of this particular incident that she's describing, the particular detail was not in the previous statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Move beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, was that the only person that you spoke to in the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't dare talk much, but she was sitting next to me and whispering to me. She told me that all this had happened there. And it's all true because there are witnesses from the school and most probably these people will come here to testify, and they themselves will be able to tell you what they saw and what they experienced. I didn't see this myself. I heard it from that woman. She also told me that Milan Lukic had taken the clothes of all the people there until they were naked and that he had forced them into a classroom, and that anything valuable that they had on them --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Same objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We don't -- do you want all this detail?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just about to finish up. This is detail -- this is greater detail than was in the statements with regard to abuse that she describes in general terms in her evidence, but I'm happy to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If it had been disclosed, that would be a different matter, but clearly it's all hearsay and undisclosed material.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm moving on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I'd like to ask you now to look around the courtroom and tell me if there is anyone --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We would object to the in-court identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I hear the objection and also from -- I take it from Mr. Cepic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I'd like to ask you to look around the courtroom please and tell me if there's anyone in this room whom you recognize in this room, other than myself and my colleagues. If you would like to stand up to have a look, you may do so, with the Chamber's permission, of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognize Sredoje and I also recognize Milan. They are sitting in the back row in the middle. Sredoje is to my right and Milan is to my left.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the record reflect that the witness has identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You may sit now, Madam Witness. Finally, can you tell the Court how these experiences have impacted you and your family.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have impacted us in the worst possible way. My heart has weakened and so has my husband's. He had to have surgery. My children suffered from trauma. I myself still suffer from trauma. Sometimes I can barely remember what my own name is. He destroyed our lives. He destroyed our health. He destroyed everything we had, Milan Lukic did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just remind us of your age, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born in 1954. I am in my 55th year of life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. My name is Jason Alarid, and I represent Milan Lukic. I'd like to ask you a few questions. Will answer my questions for me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, I'll answer about what is in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, thank you, ma'am, but we may move a little bit outside of what is exactly in your statement for purposes of this questioning. First, I'd like to just kind of follow up with a couple of things you said at the end of your testimony. One of them which is how -- that you have been so traumatized, sometimes you can hardly remember your own name. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. What I meant to say is that sometimes I don't want to live. I feel like committing suicide. I want to kill myself sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you have a maximum of one hour to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, following the war, you gave a statement -- well, actually let me ask another question. You stood up and identified my client, Milan Lukic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: On direct testimony you gave several examples of why you knew Sredoje for a long time, including the fact that he brought your husband back to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You had several long conversations with him that didn't just happen in 1992, but were over the course of many years; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you stated that you and your husband knew Sredoje for many years; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew Sredoje. He used to work in the Visegrad SUP. That's why we knew him. We knew him for the entire time of his working there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you saw him change over years and even though knowing him as a grown man, you had no trouble identifying him in court today; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The persons who socialized with us are not easy to forget.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And including the fact that you made him coffee as a reward for bringing your husband home that day; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But your husband -- you were born in 1954; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when was your husband born?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I would like to have document number -- ER number 0055-2477, and 0055-24 -- oh, that's -- excuse me, that's English and B/C/S of the witness's 1993 statement. Page 1, please. And first could we go down and match the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, is that the bottom -- at the bottom of the page there, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you recall giving a statement in 1993 to the Ministry of Internal Affairs in Gorazde; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you gave the statement a little over a year after your exodus from Visegrad; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember exactly when it was, but I do know I made the statement. Time goes by and one forgets these details.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Looking at the top of the page, ma'am, do you see December 30th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Does that refresh your recollection as to when this happened, this interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And so would it be fair to say that your memory was probably clearer just a little over a year after the incident than going on 16 years after the incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But one thing that is consistent is earlier on direct testimony, you indicated that Milan Lukic knew your husband from school; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go to the first paragraph of the bottom of the page. And I'd like you to start reading, ma'am, at "a group of aggressor soldiers." Would you read that paragraph including the name of Milan Lukic to the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just find where it is. I can't find the passage you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Let me read it for you and see if you can see as I start.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can assist, actually the B/C/S starts with [B/C/S/ spoken]. That might assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you see that, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I do. "Towards the end of May 1992, in the afternoon, a group of aggressor soldiers carrying a black flag with a skull painted on it, travelling in a few cars, arrived in my village from the direction of Prelovo in the late afternoon hours, led by Milan Lukic whom I knew personally from before as my husband's friend from school. There were about 20 of them, among whom, apart from Milan Lukic, I recognized Mitar Vasiljevic who used to work with me in the same firm. I didn't know the others, but in my opinion, the persons in question were related to Milan Lukic's family, who lived and worked on the territory of Serbia. They had mostly automatic weapons and hand grenades."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a few questions out of this. First things first, is just a year -- a little over a year after the incident you confirmed again that you knew this Milan Lukic because your husband went to school with him; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you didn't have an idea of this Milan Lukic because you had?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You didn't have an idea of this Milan Lukic because you had --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- not have an idea of who this Milan Lukic because you had known him from the town for several years; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know him from town, I knew him because he used to come and visit Emin Vila's father in my village, that's how I knew him and that's why I recognized him when he came to the village to maltreat us and persecute us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Emin Vila was born in 1955?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when Emin Vila was born, but he was a neighbour ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that he is roughly around the age of you and your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, but it was your understanding that this Milan Lukic worked with Emin Vila in Belgrade; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it would be that reason that he would visit Emin Vila because they worked together in Belgrade; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, they would come together. Milan would go to his house and Emin would go to his, but he would pass by Emin's house, and they would greet each other as colleagues and socialize as colleagues from work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if -- if -- how old is your husband today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 50 something. 51, 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that he testified in this -- in the Mitar Vasiljevic case; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not in my statement, so I won't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, he is your husband. I would assume you knew if he took a trip to The Hague to testify in a war crimes trial in 2001. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you I wouldn't discuss that. It's not in my statement, and I don't want to talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, you have to answer the question. If the question is relevant, then you are obliged to answer it to the best of your ability. If it's not relevant, I will rule it irrelevant in which case the question would not be allowed. But I can't see why you shouldn't answer this question. So what is the answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you are still married to your husband; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you confirmed in your statements to the ICTY that he in fact had already given statements to the ICTY as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And he gave statements about the same things you are talking about today, including his own abduction and arrest; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to object, but my microphone is not working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes. I don't think it's appropriate for the witness to be asked about any of the contents of what her husband testified to or what he said. She can obviously confirm whether or not she knows that he came to testify, but if the contents of her husband's evidence are going to be put to her, I would submit that the substance, the substantive matters can be put to her, factual matters, but not asking her in any way to comment upon the evidence that her husband gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: She can't say whether he gave statements about the same things, what she's talking about today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I absolutely and respectfully disagree, and the reason being is, is because these are a married couple. They gave statements to the ICTY a day apart in 2000. He testified at Mitar, she did not. In fact, he testified about the same arrest, who did it, why he knew Milan, why he knew Mitar, and the time-frames of their age and the knowledge of that. I would submit that based on his testimony, it's a different Milan, a different person and in fact he was abducted by someone other than Milan Lukic, in fact identified as a Montenegrin in his statement. We will be submitting his statements for evidence, so we can, you know, put that on the record today, but otherwise, his wife should have knowledge of that. And the fact that they diverge on very critical issues, I think is important to cross-examine this witness. Including the fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Have you asked her whether she read his statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, but I can ask her if she recognizes his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. Your question was -- you asked her whether her husband gave a statement about the same matters, abduction and so on, as she is testifying today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm saying you haven't laid any foundation --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- to establish that she has that kind of knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's what I was trying to do, and then the Prosecutor objected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Have a seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, ma'am, isn't it true that you and your husband both gave statements in May of 2000 in anticipation of possibly testifying at the Mitar Vasiljevic trial; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you travelled together; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where we travelled. You didn't tell me where we were travelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where did you give your statements in 2000, ma'am? That would maybe be easier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, to the OTP of The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were you separated for those statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And who was present for your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the investigator, myself, and an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you give your husband -- your statement before your husband, after your husband, or were you in separate rooms giving statements at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he went first, and then I gave a statement after him, on different days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were you recorded while you were being interviewed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't look to see whether they were recording, but nobody told me it was being recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So -- and how long was your interview -- how long did it take before they typed up what you had to say and memorialized it so you could, in fact, sign it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there to make a statement more than once. We couldn't complete it in one go because of the interpretation, so I had to go there several times, and after I had been there several times I signed it. After some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that your husband travelled to give another statement in 2008, this year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you go with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't necessary for me to go too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I know you gave another statement in 2006; correct? 2000, to the ICTY, I apologise, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then you gave another statement in 2006; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then you re-issued that similar statement to the Association of Women Victims of War of Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours. Could that please be redacted from the public version and could this matter please be dealt with in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are we still in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session. And that is to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that your husband knew Mitar Vasiljevic because his older brother went to school with him; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And his elder brother is one year older than your husband; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand this. There's no reference to my brother here, is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No. No, ma'am, your husband's brother. Your husband's brother went to school with Mitar Vasiljevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And your husband's brother is one year older than your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How much older is your brother's husband [sic] than he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Does that matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, I'm referring to some testimony from your husband testifying in Vasiljevic where he stated that his brother one year older than him went to school -- and we can put the transcript on the screen and we have the audio --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- and we have the audio recording of her husband testifying prepared for Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours. Again, this is asking a witness to comment on the credibility and the substance of an evidence of another witness, rather than on the substantive matter, the factual matter at hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The question I will allow is how much older is your brother's husband than he is. Can you answer that, do you know the answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My husband was born on the 30th of December, 1956. But he was registered as being born on the 5th of January, 1957, by the local notary in the book of birth. As for my brother-in-law, I don't know when he was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just from -- you've known him since you were married; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So is he about a year older, give or take a few months?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Tell us what you are trying to establish with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, as a proffer in the Mitar Vasiljevic trial, her husband testified that -- in reference to why he knew these people, one of the reference points he did is, Well, Mitar went to school with my older brother and Milan was a year behind me, being a three-year gap. These are all for gentleman born in their 50s.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. So let us hear the answer. The question was: Is he about a year older give or take a few months. Are you in a position to answer that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, because I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But as far as you knew, your husband was certain that this was a Milan that was a year younger than him and went to school in the 7th grade while he was in the 8th grade; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Again, asking the witness to establish whether or not her husband was certain about something -- she has to say what she is certain about, not what her husband or anybody else is certain about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: They lived together, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Don't ask any more questions like that. I will get annoyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking it not from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not allowing that line of questioning, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Even if it's related to her personal knowledge of her husband, not the statements. I'm not asking her about the statements. I'm asking her about have they had conversations in their household. This is a fair hearsay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You never put the question that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you want, you can put the question that way and that will provide a basis for her answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, in several statements you gave, you indicated that your husband knew Milan Lukic that day from school because he had gone to school with him; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you've discussed with your husband that relationship?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't discuss the relationship. Mitar Vasiljevic and my husband were socializing. He works in a pub as a waiter. My husband would go there and drink with him, and that's why he knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, ma'am, I was vague, I apologise. What I meant was, isn't it true that you and your husband had conversations regarding as to why your husband knew Milan Lukic went to school with him; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that you and your husband had discussions that put this Milan Lukic in the class beneath your husband, the year behind your husband, i.e., of when your husband is in 8th grade, this Milan Lukic would have been in 7th grade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What my husband was saying is that they were schoolmates but not classmates, that's what he was saying. I don't know when Milan went to school, to which class. And I don't know that my husband and Milan Lukic were classmates, because I wasn't together with my husband at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, wouldn't it be true that if Milan Lukic, in this courtroom today, were born in 1967, it would be impossible for him to be a schoolmate, much less a classmate with your husband? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be true that your husband is in a better position to know who Milan Lukic was back in 1992 than when you were?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection. Again asking the witness to assess the credibility of her husband.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: She can't comment on that. Ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Based on your knowledge of Milan Lukic in 1992, and the fact that in your 1993 statement you indicated that you knew Milan Lukic personally because your husband went to school with him, isn't it true that your husband would be in a better position to know who Milan Lukic was on that fateful day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's the same question that I just disallowed. You don't seem to understand English. I just disallowed it, so why are you putting it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand English very well. And the fact of the matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Then don't put it again. I have disallowed it and for a very good reason. Ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, isn't it true that not a single statement before 2008 in court yesterday, you never mentioned a Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did mention it. I just don't know whether that was recorded or not. Behija's Passat. Behija Zukic. I said who it belonged to, I said who took it away from her, and I said what sort of a car it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But ma'am, you never identified the Passat in any previous statement before court yesterday; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it the Passat that matters so much, is that so essential to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, ma'am. It appears to be essential to the Prosecution, and I think that's why you were asked about it. Were you prompted to talk about a Passat the day before yesterday, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who told you to talk about the Passat?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to note that the witness several times refers to a Volkswagen in her statements. The fact that she doesn't specify what kind of a Volkswagen it is is a different matter, but she does refer to Volkswagen in her statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But is there any reference to a Passat in her statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: A Passat is a kind of Volkswagen. I'm just asking the question because in the statements it clearly says a Volkswagen. There is no explicit use of the word Passat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, she'd also just identified a Golf today, so clearly she can tell the difference between make and model.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And ma'am, before the objection happened, I asked you who told you or who prompted you about the Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Tell me about that conversation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained what cars were involved, who they belonged to, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And who told you to say it was a Passat?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours. The witness didn't say that someone told her to say it was a Passat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, he did ask her who prompted her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who prompted you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So I'll allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please complete your answer, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one told me to talk about a Passat. I said it was there. No one told me. It's my statement, my evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, you realise that when you wrote down the additional witness statement of the 26th of October, 2008, you had been given an opportunity to clarify all earlier statements; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you have -- are you a special aficionado of cars, makes and models that you would know the difference between a Passat this long after the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could tell Behija's Passat. There are several kinds of Passat probably. I also owned one but it was an old model.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what would prompt you, other than the district attorney -- or excuse me, the Prosecutor reminding you of that 18 -- or, excuse me, 16 years after the fact? And why isn't it in your 2008, October 26th statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection. Again it's a mischaracterization and he hasn't actually asked her whether the Volkswagen which is mentioned, in that she meant to -- that this was the kind of Volkswagen she was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why would I lead her to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You can ask her that in re-examination, if you wish. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, ma'am, I ask again, what would prompt you, other than the Prosecutor reminding you, that 16 years after the fact and why isn't there a mention of this vehicle, make and model --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: One question at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You are right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About the Passat, for me to mention it, I mentioned it in all of my statements, the Passat that belonged to Behija Zukic. I mentioned this in all of my statements. I'm not sure if it was recorded or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, ma'am, but what I'm asking you is, what would have you identify it specifically as a Passat other than the Prosecutor telling you that? What in your own recollection clarified the make and model of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Milan Lukic himself drove it. And that's why it counts. It's important because he would drive up to our village in that Passat and he drove it himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, ma'am, I'm assuming that at the time in 1992 there were rumours about Behija Zukic, her car, and her death; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, is it the Milan Lukic that went to school with your husband that was driving that Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when did you first see Milan Lukic in uniform with Emin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, but it was a long time ago. Whenever he came, he would be wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like you to use the spring of 1992 as a reference point and go backwards from there. When was the last time before that, in as much specificity as you can, the last time that you saw Milan Lukic with Emin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, was it five months before, a year before, several years before? I mean, please help us out. You are the only one that can recall that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I can't say something that I don't know. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You lived in the same neighbourhood as the Vilas, they were your neighbours; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you said that Emin was a policeman in Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So using 1992, the spring, as a marker, when was the last time you had seen Emin in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last time, I don't know that either. Not exactly. He would come to see his aunt on a holiday. I can't remember the last time he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, had he visited at any time in the year --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was before the war. I know that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And so just for a point of reference, between June 1991 and June 1992, did you see Emin Vila at your neighbour Vila's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Between June 1991 and June 1990, going backwards in time, did you see Emin Vila at your neighbour Vila's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when he was, when it was that he last holidayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You were very clear about remembering that the Milan Lukic that went to school with your husband used to hang out with Emin Vila at their house, being your neighbours. So I'm trying to pinpoint when was the last time you saw them together, if you said you saw them there more than once?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see them together, but it was in peacetime, and then when the war in Yugoslavia broke out, not even families had an opportunity to see each other, let alone neighbours who were unrelated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Absolutely, ma'am. That's why I'm only asking you during peacetime when you remember that, so please, help me clarify. On direct examination I believe you testified that you saw Milan Lukic and Emin Vila on more than one occasion, and I need to know when that was. The Court needs to know when that was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this: I just don't know exactly. The last time they were there, I was working myself. Mustafa Vila was the one who would tell me about his visits. I may have seen him around back in 1990 or thereabouts, the last time he came, 1989, perhaps 1990, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Fair enough. And when you saw -- and did you see Milan at that time as well, 1989 or 1990?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it was your understanding that this Milan and Emin were colleagues in Belgrade; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that was colleagues at the MUP in Belgrade, correct, both police officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a place near Belgrade, perhaps part of Belgrade, I'm not sure what the name was of that place where they worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would that be Obrenovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I can't say, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that there's another witness, that's also a family member of yours, to the incidents of which you've testified besides your husband and that being your sister-in-law; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Must I answer this one? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Private session for a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that sister-in-law, her name would be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel. Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, isn't it true that your sister-in-law gave a statement on your behalf to the Women Victims Association?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on my behalf. She simply confirmed my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you request her to go there and confirm your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I needed a witness myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, just going back on something we've touched on a little bit is, did Milan Lukic wear a police uniform when you saw him before the war with Emin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both were wearing police uniforms when they came. Emin and Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I apologise. I just wanted to enter the 1993 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it. And in fact, we'll take the break now. Give us the number for the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 1D70, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long do you intend to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Not more than 5 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 5 minutes, good.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: May I start, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good day, madam. My name is Djuro Cepic, Defence counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic. I do apologise, but can you hear me? Let me just introduce myself. My name is Djuro Cepic, attorney at law, and I appear for Sredoje Lukic. Are you tired, madam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I have one question for you. Perhaps you will agree with me that Sredoje Lukic is a positive personality who in those difficult times exposed himself to danger in order to save your husband and his brother; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, very much, madam. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I'm going to quote to you a few lines from the testimony just earlier today. I'm quoting from page 32, line 19. Learned counsel for the Defence asked you the following question: "Ma'am, isn't it true that not a single statement before 2008 in court yesterday you never mentioned a Passat." Your answer was --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object. And the reason I'm objecting is simply this: When I asked that line of questioning -- what the Prosecution is going to refer to, but it's why I introduced the entire 1993 statement, is there is a mention of Passat later, after the incident. However, what I'm referring to is specifically page 111, line 10, through page 112, line 6, and it was at the questioning of Ms. Marcus stating specifically that in her statements before and referring to the BMW, VW, own car and a Yugo, the question was from the Prosecutor Ms. Marcus: "In the section you just read, you mentioned that group came from a BMW, Volkswagen" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- own car, and a Yugo, and all those -- are those the cars that you recall seeing?" "Answer: I saw -- well, was Behija Zukic's Passat in a burgundy colour, but it's not mentioned there and the car was driven by Milan Lukic." So I was specifically relating to that time period not to later in the time period, because that's what, of course, what I'm going to be arguing in my submission that in fact she was prompted to inject the Passat because in that same statement which was introduced into evidence she specifically refers to Milan Lukic, the Milan Lukic that she knew, coming, this time, in the car from Behija Zukic, after the fact that she described the four vehicles. So it implies that, in fact, this Milan Lukic changed cars after what she had testified to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So what is your point, that she -- that it doesn't arise or that -- why can't she ask about the Passat since it was raised in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I know what they are going to imply, they are going to imply that, in fact, what I was arguing in my questioning, and I was arguing specifically related to the time when Milan Lukic first came up in a group of cars, where she identified the VW, the BMW and a couple of others.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may be a little premature because we haven't even heard the specific question. She merely identified the passage from your cross-examination. What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd also like to respond to that. There is nothing whatsoever in that line of questioning which identified to the witness which portion was related to, and counsel put two direct, broad-sweeping questions to the witness. The first one was what I was just about to read: "Ma'am, isn't it true that not a single statement before 2008 in court yesterday you never mentioned a Passat." And her response was: "I did mention it. I just don't know whether that was recorded or not. Behija's Passat. Behija Zukic. I said who it belonged to and I said who took it away from her and I said what kind of a car it was." Immediately following that, counsel again put the question to her: "But, ma'am, you never identified the Passat in any previous statement before court yesterday; isn't that true?" There was no reference to any particular portion of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You both seem to be ready for a little fight. I just want to hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. For the question, I would like to up Exhibit 1D70. It was just admitted. Perhaps the document ID number would be helpful, that would be 0055-2477, and its corresponding English translation. The first part I'd like to go to is on the English page 2 at the bottom. On the B/C/S page 3 at the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, can you see the statement on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you kindly read for us one line which at the top of the page which starts with the words: "Milan Lukic came back to our village again that same day."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Milan Lukic came back the same day. This time he was alone in a car taken from Behija Zukic from Visegrad. He was armed with a submachine gun and" --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to now turn to page 5 in the English at the bottom, and page 5 in the B/C/S in the middle. Madam, do you see a line in the middle of the page which starts with the words "during my stay at Bikavac"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my stay at Bikavac, I can't say exactly, 19 days on several occasions, Milan Lukic, Vidoje Andric, came in a Passat car, dark red in colour, and brought younger women and the girls to be raped. I remember Besima from Medjudja, a schoolmate of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Witness. And my question is: Mr. Alarid was not correct when he said that you had not made mention of a Passat in your previous statements; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Cause for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How so? Either it's there in the statement or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because again, Your Honour, that was the whole point of my earlier objection. I introduced the entire statement making the point there was reference to the day. The fact is, is in her 2008 statement -- excuse me, 2006, is when she brought up describing the cars that these gentlemen came to on that first day. In fact, on page 1 of this exhibit, she identifies simply a bunch of cars and then creates the differential of -- that when Milan Lukic comes it's in a -- almost implying that it's in a different car than was there earlier. Yet at the prompting of the Prosecution, the Passat now is there from the very, very beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not even certain whether the question is necessary because the Judges would have seen the statement and we able to read.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution now calls VG-133. Mr. Cole will be handling this witness. Your Honour, this witness is the same situation as we had with VG-064. It's a witness that we already put forward as a 92 ter witness, but in going over the Court decisions we were not able to find where the Court explicitly granted that. So our application --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I checked on that. I am a now ready for this, Mr. -- I am now for it. I checked with my legal officers and no application was made for 92 ter. No application, that is my information which I just had from the legal officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, then I stand corrected, Your Honour. I apologise to the Chamber and would the Chamber entertain an oral 92 ter submission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I would. I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I'd ask Mr. Cole to deal with that. Your Honour, I do want to say, before it gets too far away from us, I do want to place on the record my very strong objection to what has just happened. It's happened a few times before in the case and we all make mistakes when we cite to a record and we make oversights, but I think in this particular case, such a direct question that it wasn't in the statement and then followed by an entire line of questions impugning the integrity of Ms. Marcus, that she had somehow prompted the witness to identify the car as a Passat, I can't sit by here silent as the integrity of my staff, who I have the highest faith in their integrity, is called into question. I would ask Mr. Alarid to please be more cautious before he levels such a serious accusation impugning the integrity of a member of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we don't want to have another discourse on this, but Mr. Alarid. Just very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I mean I've got to say tunnel vision sometimes works that way, but I was focused on the statement which Ms. Marcus left at the end of the day yesterday which was acknowledging that the statements had never mentioned the Passat before and was asking for a clarification and making that point, I believe, and I would make that point in my submissions as well. Although, I would raise that the fact that these we receiving multiple proofing notes in the days before these things and very simple matters but yet very pointed matters such as dates and makes and models of cars are coming into complete clarity after over a decade of time is troubling to me because that's just not the way my understanding of human memory usually works.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Alarid. The next witness, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Before the witness is brought in, I have in fact two applications to make. The first one just referred to by Your Honour a short time ago, the 92 ter. I've certainly prepared to deal with this witness by way of 92 ter. We did make --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the estimate for the witness as viva voce?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, viva voce it would be, I don't know, maybe 2 or 3 hours. 92 ter, I am hoping something like three-quarters of an hour. Could I just mention, sir, that when we made the application, Your Honour, to include this witness amongst the Prosecution witnesses, we did file a summary of the witness together with the mode of testimony mentioned 92 ter at that stage, and with the evidence in chief listed at .5 of an hour. I think Your Honour granted the application in relation to this witness and one other witness without referring to the mode of testimony at that stage. So we've assumed that it would be a 92 ter, and certainly in the circumstances, I would ask now that I be able to proceed with the 92 ter procedure with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Alarid has something to say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour. I mean the problem I have is is that on the October 21st memorandum to all parties, the Court included, it -- the OTP listed this witness as viva voce. For one. Secondarily, we've received two proofing notes. One the 28th of October, 2008, listing 15 changes in relation to the paragraphs, and then at 2.15 today we received a second proofing note with seven additional changes. So how can we go 92 ter on a statement that's being modified so drastically at the very tail end of the process? In other words, limiting our cross based on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But you would be able to cross-examine on the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are the proofing notes allowed to come in as evidence? I mean at the last witness, Witness 64, they made these proofing statements into amended statement. In this particular case it wasn't transcended into a statement. We made a motion for a proofing note to come in at some point, and I think that it would be appropriate that the proofing note come in as part of the statement under that argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll leave it to Mr. Cole to -- with respect to the proofing note but I don't imagine that we would object to a proofing note. Just so that it's clear, when witnesses are brought here, and one of virtues that I believe the -- why the rules were changed to accommodate 92 ter, was that witnesses could be brought to The Hague, we'd have an opportunity to look at their statement, and then could advise the Chamber whether there's anything they wished to change. When the witnesses arrive here, typically two days before, the day before their testimony they are given an opportunity to read their statement and anything that they say that is -- that they believe is a correction, we are duty-bound to disclose that to the counsel, and also duty-bound to raise it in the foundation of 92 ter. I can think of no other way to deal with the matter. As we heard with VG-064, aside from the new assault, and she gave her explanation as to why that wasn't included, they were all very minor inconsistencies or minor changes, none of them that had any direct bearing on a material issue in this case. The change of the word from "toward Visegrad" from "to Visegrad," and the change of the spelling of the word Prelovo. They were minor corrections but ones that we are required to deal with. So there is nothing, I believe, that prejudices the Defence with respect to this. The total amount of material is less than two pages. Mr. Alarid has had it shortly after the witness has said it to us. I can't imagine that we can get that information to him any quicker, and he has a full opportunity to cross-examine the witness on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the proofing note would be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In this case, if Mr. Alarid feels that fairness requires that, I would no objection to that. We tried to do that yesterday and there was vehement objection to it. So whichever way the Chamber wishes to conduct the trial, the Prosecution will be happy to accommodate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I guess my concern is, you know, just given the previous objection, and I object -- you objected to dumping yesterday; I object assault, if that's the case. But other than that, the issue is simply this, is we need time to prepare, Your Honour. And when the witnesses are changing their testimony and changing statements and at this late hour and yet they are coming in 92 ter, it gives us very little time to adjust for those changes in cross-examination. And even the Court saying, Well, you have the opportunity to cross-examine, it's what makes those mistakes like I just made, that failure to clarify the separation of semantics in the earlier statement is exactly what I'm talking about because before yesterday, Your Honour, that client -- that witness had not mentioned Passat anywhere in relation to this first encounter with Mr. Lukic and didn't identify this car, and all of a sudden, it pops into the fray, not even part of the proofing note. And it makes it very difficult for us to adjust in a 92 ter scenario because it does change how we prepare as opposed to a viva voce witness. That is the nature of our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just point out, unless there is another alternative what the witness tells us we try to get that information as quickly as possible to the Defence. I can think of no other alternative. I'm happy to hear suggestions from either Mr. Alarid or the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm just reading the 92 ter rule, Your Honour, I just can't understand how we can do it when the details of the statements have now changed. And just looking at the most recent proofing note, the changes include people being there and not being there, including description issues. Those kinds of things are changing. If the description and number of people change, how can this be 92 ter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
