utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, the Chamber will admit the statement under 92 ter. If you are in any way embarrassed by the lateness of changes in these statements to the extent that they go to material issues, then you can bring that to our attention, and the Chamber will deal with it. Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There was one further application and it relates to protective measures for this witness that I would ask that we deal with in private session before the witness is brought in, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session. Now being operated by the court deputy. When we move to private session, apparently she needs a little time for the -- for certain matters to be attended to.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. And you may begin, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could the court usher pass the pseudonym sheet to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Witness VG-133.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: You can hear me clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: You have been granted protective measures by the Court in the form of screening from the public, facial distortion and the use of a pseudonym, and your pseudonym is VG-133. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: On the piece of paper before you, can you confirm that your name and date of birth are correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you please sign that pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And I ask that the pseudonym sheet be entered into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P160, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could I now ask that the court usher provide the witness with a pseudonym reference sheet. Your Honour, I note Mr. Cepic is looking a bit mused. I can indicate that one of the persons on the reference sheet with a pseudonym is not currently on the witness list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please clarify which witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-133, this reference sheet in front you contains the names of persons or may mention or be asked about in your testimony. Next to their names are pseudonyms for them. I would ask if you could kindly use the pseudonym instead of the name of the person if you refer to either of these persons during your testimony. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-133, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim. A Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And in which municipality in Bosnia-Herzegovina were you born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, as VG-133 is a 92 ter witness, I'll now proceed to confirm her prior statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-133, did you provide a written statement to an ICTY investigator on the 18th and 20th of August, 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Was this statement typed in English at the time, read back to you in the Bosnian language, and did you sign the English version?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity this week to review that statement in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And on reviewing the statement, did you find some items in your statement which needed to be corrected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness could be shown her statement in B/C/S. The ERN number is 06382732 to 06382740. The English statement has the same numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you see a copy of the B/C/S, of the Bosnian version of your statement on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Refer you to paragraph 6 of your statement where you describe the date you finished work at the Visegrad Health Centre, and where it indicates you stopped work in the middle of May of 1992. What date did you actually finish work at the centre in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: On the 26th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And after that date, did you return and finally finish on a later date in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What was the actual final day that you worked at the Visegrad Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: The 31st of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Would you have a look now, please, at paragraph 9 of your statement where it indicates that Dr. Vasiljevic said that you could go. Can you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: In English -- oh, yes. Yes, now I see it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Should that in fact read that Dr. Vasiljevic took Milan Lukic out of the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: No, it says here that he said I should leave the room, but that's not correct. Dr. Vasiljevic took Milan Lukic out of the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Also on paragraph 9, there is a passage that says that Milan Lukic had colours on his face occasionally but very rarely. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So does that need to be corrected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes. He never had any colours on his face that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'll now refer you to paragraph 17 to 20 of your statement. These are paragraphs of your statement where you are describing an incident where Milan Lukic visited your mother-in-law's apartment building in Visegrad, took away some neighbours, and killed them on the nearby bridge. Do you see those paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I have paragraph 18 right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So my question in relation to those paragraphs is: What date do you now say it was that this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: On the 10th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is -- my objection is this is exactly what I'm talking about. See, and the reason being is this: In the proofing note we just got today there's seven enumerated items. In the proofing note we got yesterday there's 15 enumerated items. In the proofing note of yesterday, in contrast to the one today, there's no identification to which paragraph, what line, that the witness is in fact clarifying. As opposed to the one today, which makes a minor change. For instance, number 4, in relation to paragraph 20, the ERN number should read 5160, not 5061. That makes perfect sense to me. But in this particular case, we are going to her statement, which you have before you, which gives a little description of an incident in where someone supposedly abducted and then killed. There's no date in reference to that whatsoever. Above it in paragraph 17, there's a relationship to in June 1992, Milan Lukic. And then it goes on to a little bit more description. I don't believe there's another date referenced on that page until the bottom, paragraph 20, which says the 7th of June. And that's somehow how this witness referenced or actually believed that something occurred in relation to the entry in the book. In the original statement it appears, if you look to paragraph 20, she relates the exact date that she can't be sure to June 7th. Well, yet in the proofing note, I am assuming this is what Mr. Cole is going to refer to, it specifically states that, Well, I'd previously suspected June 7th, but now she knows it was June 10th because that was the day she found her mother and the same day her husband told her he had seen men taken to from the Varda factory and to the river and killed. Four days later, her mother was expelled from Visegrad. That's a great amount of detail covering days, covering Varda, which wasn't even in the statement. Correct me if I'm wrong, is Varda mentioned in the original statement from 2008, I didn't see it. But now we are now triangulating this to now incorporate Varda? And what, is this witness now become an alibi rebuttal? I mean, the fact of the matter is, is that is much more substantive than the normal 92 process. This involves groups of new testimony of which I can't get into but for there being a statement that says it in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We are left with the words of the witness during a proofing over the last two days. There are obligations that follow on from disclosures by the witness, as Mr. Groome has said. Now, what I'm attempting to do here, because it's a 92 ter process, is to briefly go through whether there are any matters in the paragraphs of the statement that the witness needs to correct, because she's going to be asked with these corrections what -- are the contents of the statement true and correct. So I'm going through briefly each of the matters, there aren't a lot of them, and counsel has been notified of them, and going to deal with them a little bit more in a little bit more depth later on. But this is for the purposes of 92 ter at the moment. Now, the matters that my learned friend raises are matters that he can properly put to the witness during cross-examination. If there have been changes, as there have been, it's a matter for cross-examination, not a matter for an objection at this stage when we are validating a 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: His point is that coming at this stage, he would not have had sufficient time to prepare for such a substantive change.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, certainly, Your Honours, some of the changes to the statement and he has mentioned another one where it's a matter of a number, I will be dealing with the changes. They are changes. We are stuck with them and have to deal with them, and he will have the opportunity to cross-examine. If he needs some time for a particular change, he can make an appropriate application to the Court for some time to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have heard Mr. Alarid, and essentially the whole purpose of this exercise really is to determine prejudice, if there's prejudice to the Defence. And if the Defence persuades the Trial Chamber that it will be prejudiced, then we'll take appropriate action. But we haven't reached that stage yet. You can carry out your cross-examination, and then if you wish, you can make an appropriate application to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the only -- I'd ask guidance from the Court, is in the 92 ter scenario with this proofing note, which I've had my assistant go get some copies of because I think the Court is entitled to see, it's impossible to cross-examine this. And what the 92 ter scenario is it allows him to lead the witness through very substantive issues including dates and new murders and killings and knowledge of murders that may not have been mentioned in other places, now they are coming in through a proofing note which technically is not signed or affirmed by this witness, and yet this Prosecutor gets to then lead the witness through very substantive things. So it circumvents the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 92 ter is an abbreviated procedure. It's purpose really is to advance the proceedings more quickly, but there must not be any prejudice to the Defence or to the other side because the Defence also has the same opportunity to make use of the procedure. You speak of leading the witness. On the 92 ter the statement is presented, so what the Prosecutor does or the party relying on it does is simply to bring to the attention of the Chamber certain important features from that statement. So it's not -- it's a statement that is in lieu of examination-in-chief. So please bear that in mind, it's in lieu of examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. And all I can say is reading the -- yesterday's proofing note, this is a more of a new statement than a corrections of minor technical inaccuracies. This is a new statement involving very new accusations and very new affirmations of which the only way he is allowed under 92 ter is technically to lead. Isn't it true you made this change, and yes, I made this change. And yet there's not even a reference to specific paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you have a hard copy that I can look at, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Your Honour. And the Court did receive a copy of it, I can indicate, as part of the list that was disseminated. Can I just indicate - I'll provide Your Honour with one now - that we are prepared, if necessary, to ask the witness to return if some prejudice can be demonstrated by my learned friend at some stage, and needs further time to cross-examine the witness. That's one of the options that is available.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Other than that, Your Honour, we have no objection to the statement itself coming in, because I think that's proper. So, you know, from the technical side I have no objection to the statement. It's really what happened in the proofing session that leaves me unable to figure out how to handle the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I am a little troubled when I see this, is it a proofing, they are proofing note. The witness related the following additional information, and you have some 15 matters dealt with. Now, there isn't even one that is of the same species as identified by Mr. Groome earlier, changing "to" to "toward." They all seem to deal with relatively substantial or material matters. It seems to be something new, though, Mr. Groome, because I can't remember, for example, when you appeared in Slobodan Milosevic, a trial in which I participated, I don't remember our having this experience where, you know, we had what virtually amounts to another statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think there is some explanation given the unique nature of this case, if I might explain. This witness is called in alibi rebuttal, so the witnesses that the Prosecution had identified earlier on and/or the matter of original witness list, I had sent out the lawyers to meet with the witnesses in the spring and the summer, and any changes in their statements was noted and disclosed to Defence counsel. As this witness is one of the witnesses that -- these alibi rebuttal witnesses we've primarily identified on statements and they have not been spoken to for some period of time with respect from the Prosecution, although some witnesses I did attempt to send Prosecution staff out to meet the witness. I'm not sure whether this particular witness was one of the people that was met in the field. But we are stuck with the problem, Your Honour, of when the witness comes and we interview the witness, the witness may provide additional information. We try to present this in the balanced way. If you will note on the proofing summary, this witness said during the session that on the 14th of June she did not see Sredoje Lukic there. Obviously a very important piece of information for the Sredoje Lukic Defence. So we tried to present the information to the Defence as soon as we obtain it. But we really have no other option, when the witness tells us something, to provide that information and to act accordingly. I would, as Mr. Cole has already said, it would seem to me that at the conclusion of the examination today, if the Court feels that fairness requires the witness to return, I'm sure she would oblige the Chamber and return for whatever additional questions that Mr. Alarid puts forward as fairness requires and the Chamber might deem fairness requires.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We are going to proceed on the basis that if the Defence feels in any way that is embarrassed or prejudiced by the lateness of this information, then it may make an appropriate application at the appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: One thing there Mr. Ivetic brought to my attention was more practical but really common sensical, is that nothing is provided in the language of the witness that allows us to put it to the witness in any way, shape or form in this environment. So we don't have a translation that we can put side by side on the screen and then allow the witness to say is that really what you said yesterday in your proofing statement. So it makes it very difficult and it allows for things to be lost in translation here in court today because then I'm forced to read from what is put in English, and then I think it's almost leading because then it gives incentive to the witness to agree in some way that this is what she said. And the accused also has a right to receive it in its own language.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's just technically not possible when a witness says something in the morning they're to testify to have the translation in written form. Whenever we can, we do do that, as we did with VG-064, and we rely on the interpretation, interpreters in court to interpret the English information as provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the only other issue is, Your Honours, is it was my understanding that this witness was brought in alibi rebuttal. And specifically, I saw it as somewhat cumulative because I believe, and I forget the VG so I won't say it, but the nurse that already authenticated the protocol book, and so I was wondering why this wasn't going to be considered cumulative, and then I notice that now it's starting to move to, well, I guess it's alibi rebuttal for Varda but that's brought to us in testimony technically because we received it at 2.15. And I would believe that's wholly improper and the witness should be stricken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will not, as you call it, strike the witness. We'll proceed in the manner that I have outlined. Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether you are addressing to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I said we will not accede to the request to do what Mr. Alarid has called striking the witness. We will not strike the witness. We'll proceed in the manner that I have outlined.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-133, I'm referring to the paragraphs in your statement where you are describing an incident where Milan Lukic visited your mother-in-law's apartment building in Visegrad and took away some neighbours and killed them on the nearby bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But it's in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But in context with the proofing session, I mean, it really amounts to leading, Judge. I can't think of any other way to characterize it when this is brought in at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What paragraph is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm asking the witness, now, Your Honour, about paragraphs 17 to 20 in her statement which describes a particular incident, and I'm going to ask her what date does she now say that incident occurred. And as Your Honours indicated, the statement is part of the evidence or will be shortly, pursuant to 92 ter and it's a matter that has arisen in proofing and needs to be clarified now as part of the 92 ter procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please answer the question. Do you want to have it repeated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The incident you describe in your statement in paragraphs 17 to 20 where you were describing an incident where Milan Lukic visited your mother-in-law's apartment building in Visegrad, took away some neighbours and killed them on the nearby bridge, what date do you now believe that that incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: The 10th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And specifically on paragraph 17, it's about the same incident, what time of the day do you now believe the killings on the bridge by Milan Lukic occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Between 1800 and 1900 hours in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Moving on to paragraph 20 of your statement, the first line where it refers to the protocol book entry number 5061, do you confirm that the entry should in fact read 5160?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Paragraph 24 of your statement where it says there that you were warned by the wife of Dr. Uljarevic, should that in fact read you were warned by Dr. Uljarevic himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Finally paragraph 25, describing an incident after the burial of Behija Zukic, and in this paragraph it mentions that Sredoje Lukic and Milan Lukic's brother were present. Should that in fact read that you did not see Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't and I don't know that man was Milan Lukic's brother. That's what the passers-by said, I wasn't sure myself, I didn't know him. So maybe it was or maybe it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, with the corrections that we have just dealt with, do you confirm that the statement you made on the 18th and 20th of August, 2008, is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And if I were to ask you the same questions today, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: They would.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honour, I would tender the statement of VG-133 into evidence, pursuant to Rule 92 ter under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P161, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-133, where were you working in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: The health centre in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: At that time had you worked there for a number of years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: 14, to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the protocol books used to record patient visits to the Visegrad Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would object as cumulative to testimony regarding the protocol book considering it's already been entered into evidence and also authenticated by another qualified witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the book has been authenticated. I'm going to be referring the witness to specific extracts, which are now in electronic form, from the book. It's not a matter of authenticating the book as such. In fact, the book isn't in court. The witness is going to be referring to specific extracts, and as a preliminary matter, I have just asked her if she's familiar with the protocol books being used at the Visegrad Health Centre, which in my submission, is entirely appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the protocol books used to record patient visits to the Visegrad Health Centre in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And were you shown copies of pages from the protocol book from the Visegrad Health Centre during your interview with Mr. Caine from ICTY in August 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And were you shown copies of certain entries in the book for May and June of 1992 in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And were you shown copies of pages from May and June of 1992 during your proofing yesterday and today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you confirm that these were authentic copies of the pages of the actual protocol book as you knew it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And did you in fact identify some of your own handwriting in some of the entries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And did you see entries in relation to persons whom you knew who attended the health centre in May and June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: We are going to see that shortly when I refer the witness to specific extracts from the Visegrad Health Centre protocol book. And these extracts have been listed on the exhibit list that was submitted, I think, last week and which counsel have copies of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. We'll get to that then.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. And I can indicate, Your Honour, that I'm going to be showing the witness three selections of copies of pages from the protocol book and asking that they be admitted into evidence and be given exhibits numbers. I'm going to ask that the witness be shown an entry number 4811 on the 20th of May, 1992. So if she could be shown the first of two pages --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection to anything on the 20th of May, 1992, as being not relevant, outside the period of the indictment, and not related to alibi rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But the fact that is outside the period of indictment doesn't by itself make it irrelevant. Let me hear Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Sir, the 20th of May, we'll hear, is an entry in the health -- Visegrad Health Centre book which give details of Behija Zukic, the body of Behija Zukic being brought into that centre on that day. There will be further testimony about her car on that day, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I want to ask you, VG-133, about an entry 4811 on the 20th of May, 1992, in relation to Behija Zukic. I'm going to be asked that you be shown first -- firstly, the first of two pages, 0545, this is ERN number, 2003. Right. At the top of the page, entry number 4811, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the date recorded is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: The 20th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the address given is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Dusce.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown -- well, before we go there. Can you confirm that the each entry in relation to a patient extends across two pages in the Visegrad centre health [sic] protocol book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If we could now have a look at 05452004. Right. Can you see this page before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you please read out the other entries relating to Behija Zukic which you can see on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: "Brought in at 8.30 to the morgue in an ambulance. Dr. Vasiljevic established death, Jamak Huso and Amir Omerovic accompanying."

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you know the person named in this entry, Behija Zukic, before this day, the 20th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How well did you know her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I knew her well. She had a private shop, a privately owned shop in Visegrad near Risavski [phoen] bridge, so everybody knew her.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, the entry that you've just been shown gives the date of 20 May 1992. Do you know what date it was that Behija Zukic was actually killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I don't know on what day she was killed, but she was killed in the course of that night. We were told in the morning at 7.30 by telephone. I answered the phone when it rang. A male voice introduced himself as calling from the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: He gave us the address and he said that there was a dead woman lying across the threshold of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, did Behija Zukic own a car, that you were aware of, in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What sort of car was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: It was a Passat. Dark red colour Passat.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And did you see her car on the day her body was brought into the Visegrad Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Who was driving her car that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: On that day our driver, Marijan Markovic from the health centre, went to collect the body of this dead female person in Dusce, and when he approached the health centre in the ambulance, a dark red Passat was following the ambulance. And as he was parking the ambulance next to the health centre, the car of Behija Zukic also parked and Milan Lukic was at the wheel. He was driving it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Was there anyone sitting next to Milan Lukic in the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Next to Milan Lukic was a former policeman, Niko Vujicic. And on the seat behind was Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you look at Milan Lukic himself in the driver's seat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes. We all looked at him as we were taking Behija Zukic's body. It was wrapped in a blanket. And as we were taking it out of the ambulance, he was maybe at a distance of 1 metre away from us. He opened the window of the door and he laughed cynically, looking out through the window of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that the electronic copies of the two pages of the protocol book for the 20th of May, just shown to the witness, be tendered into evidence as an exhibit, 05452003 and 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P162, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour, that they need to be under seal. We have blocked out the names of the patient, the patients and their -- of course, Behija Zukic, her name was necessarily left uncovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We would prefer an unredacted copy under seal so that maybe handwriting can be compared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll keep them under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, had you at any stage ever been introduced to this man Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Who introduced you to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Dr. Radomir Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you just give us the brief circumstances of how you were introduced to Milan Lukic by the doctor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: It happened in mid-May, approximately. I know it was a working day, and Milan Lukic brought along a soldier for his hand to be bandaged, and he was in the room where we did this all the time. I looked at the wound on that soldier's arm and I called Dr. Vasiljevic to take a look at it. Dr. Vasiljevic came in, he greeted Milan Lukic, and asked me if I knew him. I said I didn't, and then he said, "This is Milan Lukic."

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Which year -- you've told us it was May, which year was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: It was in mid-May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And how long was Milan Lukic in your presence on that day, the day of the introduction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I can't be precise, but it might have been 10 or 15 minutes because the intervention in the case of that soldier was only 5 or 6 minutes long. It wasn't a complicated job. And when we finished, Milan Lukic turned towards me, he showed me his hands, and he asked me, What about me? His hands were covered with blood. And I showed him the tap where he could wash his hands and he objected to that. And then Dr. Vasiljevic intervened and said he could easily do that, there was no problem. He asked us to disinfect his hands, but after he had washed his hands, when he had washed the blood off his hands, there were no injuries to be seen on his hands. I told him there was no need to do anything, and then he said, It's your responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When you say, "He asked us to disinfect his hands," who is that "he"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, after the death of Behija Zukic, did you ever see Milan Lukic driving around town in a car?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you ever see Milan Lukic driving around? Did you ever see Milan Lukic driving around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was he driving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A dark red Passat belonging to Behija Zukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you ever see anyone else in the driver's seat of Behija Zukic's Passat vehicle around Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Never did I see anyone except Milan Lukic driving it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How many times would you have seen Milan Lukic driving that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: There was hardly a day when we didn't see him. I couldn't tell you the number of times, but it was almost daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Over a period of how many days or months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: From the 20th of May until the 17th of June, 1992, when I left Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask now if the witness could be shown copies of four pages from the protocol book commencing with ERN 05452039.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you see the page before you that contains entries numbered 4991 through to 5000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes, but it's all black.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We would ask that unredacted copies be shown to the witness and if privacy issues are -- we could keep it under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If I could just have a moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If I could just have a moment. If we are going to show this unredacted, it would need to be in private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We just had Exhibit P163 under seal entered into evidence. Could I ask that the unredacted version -- could I ask that the redacted version also be entered as an exhibit, which is ERN 05452039 to 2042. That's the redacted version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P164, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now going to ask that the witness be shown, finally, in relation to the protocol book, six pages. And if we are going to do it, Your Honour, in the unredacted version, if I could ask that the witness be shown the first two pages -- sorry, ERN number 05452071. And if I could ask if we could have side by side page 270 and the following page 271. In fact, I'm advised that it's the same ERN number that is on the screen at the moment, but if we could go to page 270 on the left-hand side and the subsequent page on the right-hand side. Right, we have the right page on the left-hand side. Could we have it the other way around, please, with the entry numbers 2071 on the left-hand side. All right. We seem to be there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Witness VG-133, can you see before you a page from the book starting with entry 5151?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If we go down to entry 5156, what is the date alongside that entry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: 7 June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And does that appear to be the first entry for the 7th of June that day, the entry 5156?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What was the earliest time that that person, the first entry on the 7th of June, 1992, would have been seen by staff at the emergency department?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Because the 7th of June was a Sunday and only the emergency ward was operating on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, if we could see on the screen, please, the next two consecutive pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the page on the right-hand side, can you have a look at the page on the left-hand side. Does that show the next number of patients for the 7th of June in sequence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And if we could see the very last entry on that page on the left-hand side. Can you see item -- entry number 5170 at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What is the name that appears alongside entry 5170?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What is alongside the entry for Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: It says: "Member of the ETO, examined by a doctor, received two shots."

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Now can we look at the right-hand page. Can you see the entry there relating to Milan Lukic in terms of treatment?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is cumulative. It's already in evidence and already been testified to by the other nurse witness. And also personal knowledge, Your Honour, she testified that she left the Visegrad Health Centre May 31st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is the cumulative character of the evidence a ground for objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, from the perspective of personal knowledge, I think it adds to the objective -- objection, but necessarily we don't need more than one person to authenticate a particular document. And given the fact that she wasn't at work on June 7th, I think it's not the best evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why do you need this evidence from her, Mr. Cole?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask that the witness read out the entry of treatment for Milan Lukic, and the situation is this: You will hear that it indicates there was intramuscular and/or intravenous injections administered. I'm going to ask the witness, where in the normal scheme of things at this health centre, such injections were administered to the patients which has relevance in other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's not how this witness was disclosed, and otherwise, she's not been tendered as an expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it's not clear to me that she is going to give evidence as an expert, that she's giving expert evidence. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you just read out the treatment, the items on the right-hand page in relation to what happened with Milan Lukic on the 7th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: It was about bronchitis, that's what he received treatment for, according to the code here. Two antibiotics were administered as well as glucosis and vitamins.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How were these things administered to the patient? Does it say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes. It says medical examination and then below that intramuscular in the first instance, and intravenous in the other instance. These are abbreviations.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So as of 1992 when you were working there, how was such injections or where were such injections administered to the body of the patient? What part of the body?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for speculation. Lack of personal knowledge and she has not been tendered as an expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You'll have to lay a foundation for that, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Had you yourself experience over the years of the administration of intramuscular and intravenous injections to patients at the Visegrad Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we will object. It was not part of the Rule 65 ter summary and not -- no motion to amend was timely filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 65 ter is only a summary. Proceed, and let us hear how she would have acquired -- how and why she would have acquired that knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Over the years that you worked at the Visegrad Health Centre, what experience did you have with the administration of intramuscular or intravenous injections to patients who reported to the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: That was our job. Every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you do this yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Hundreds of times a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Now, where were such injections administered? What part of the patient's body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: For the most part with adult men the cubital vein, that was the intravenous injection, the muscular to the gluteal muscle.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So, the intravenous injections were normally administered to the inside of the elbow, the arm at the inside of the elbow you indicated to the Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Just ask that the witness be shown the final two pages next in sequence. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Do you see before you the next two pages in sequence from the protocol book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So does this -- this page on the left-hand side show the final entry for the 7th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Indeed it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And what is that entry number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: 5179, if my reading is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So 5179, the last entry for the 7th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, can you see entry 5180 with the date the 8th of June alongside it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What would be the earliest time on the 8th of June that a patient -- that the patient at entry 5180 could have been attended to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: If one just worked straight on as we normally did, and there were no changes, this patient could have been admitted after 1500 hours, 3.00 p.m. on the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And finally, I'm going to ask you about two entries in particular. Entries 5178 and 5179, can you see those entries on the pages before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, looking at the entries for 5178 and 5179, can you see any time written alongside those entries which indicates the time those persons were seen at the Visegrad Health Centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What time does it indicate there that these persons were seen on the date that they are entered there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: 7th of June, 0030. Half past midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would object to this. And one, if the witness can mark it, but other than that, we would object to the tendering of this evidence as not relevant, not properly disclosed, and otherwise, I mean, what is the purpose? Lack of personal knowledge, the witness was not there. The document speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: It will be a matter for the Trial Chamber in due course, of course, Your Honour. I'm asking the witness to relate to the Court what is written in the protocol book, not her interpretation of it. What is written there. And the Defence will have any opportunity to challenge this if they so wish. She is relating to the Court what she can see on the pages before the Court as to the timing of the entry in the book for the two entry numbers 5178 and 5179, which is entirely appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, I've just about finished with this area, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: VG-133, although entries 5178 and 5179 are included under the 7th of June, having read the times of half past midnight, what does that indicate in terms of which day the entries were made?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for speculation, and why didn't the first witness that authenticated this and interpreted it -- these results, touch on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let her provide first a basis for her knowledge, if she has any.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Looking at the items that indicate the time the patients were seen was 0030 hours, what experience do you have in recording items in the protocol book or reading the protocol book to be able to tell which particular day the timing refers to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, it calls for speculation, anything after May 31st, for that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let her answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These patients were recorded in relation to the 7th of June, 1992. The reason being at the time this was the way patients were recorded. They would be recorded for that particular shift. For example, this was a Sunday, it was between 7.00 in the morning that Sunday and 7.00 in the morning the next day. Regardless of the fact that this occurred on the 8th of June, it was past midnight so it was the 8th of June already. The patient was recorded under the 7th of June simply because it occurred during the same shift as the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Have you counted up the entries for the 7th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I think there were a total of 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Right. And the entry --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: If my count is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the entry for Milan Lukic was at what number of those entries, of the 24?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I think 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask now, Your Honour, if the six pages the witness has referred to could be tendered into evidence as an exhibit under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P165, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And could I ask that the redacted copies that are contained on the Prosecution's exhibit list be tendered as an exhibit also. Those are ERN 05452071-1 to 0545-2076.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P166, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Which bridge did the killings occur on?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: It's not a leading question, with respect, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I'm giving some thought to these objections as to the leading character of the evidence on Rule 92. Rule 92 is an abbreviated procedure which is in lieu of evidence in chief. So ordinarily the statement is tendered. When a statement is tendered, no question arises as to whether anything is leading or not. So the procedure which counsel goes through at this particular time is merely to identify points of interest in that statement. So it's not clear to me how leading arises, because this really is a statement in lieu of examination-in-chief. And it appears to me that if you have an objection, it's really to the whole procedure of Rule 92 ter --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I will admit -- I will admit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- and you may very well be on some fair ground there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's been the troubling thing especially with the proofing notes and the changes related to this alleged incident, especially involving this witness's supposed witnessing of these deaths. And it still strikes me as leading when the Prosecutor suggests, i.e., killing in a question, it does lead because it take that witness straight to the point, and I guess maybe that is the point of the procedure and I'm having the hardest time grasping that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If he had said to her, in your statement you referred to a killing, so and so, I mean, that would not be objectionable in terms of the procedure under Rule 92 ter. So you are either going to accept 92 ter or you don't. If you don't accept it, then you can take that up somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What did you see happened to the four men that I mentioned on the bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Milan Lukic killed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Where did you watch that from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: From a balcony that was in the flat of my mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Which bridge are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: The old one, the old Visegrad bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What was the distance from the balcony to where you saw Milan killing the men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Perhaps between 200 and 300 metres as the crow flies. 300 metres. Thereabouts, if you take the road to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What date did you see this happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: 10th of June. 1992, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What are the events, if any, that help you fix the date at the 10th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I was able to remember the date because my mother had gone missing several days before. My sister and I had no idea about her whereabouts since the Sunday before. On the 10th of June, which was a Wednesday as it happens, the two of us headed for my mother's village to look for her. Previously, we had been informed that women had been killed in that village, five or six of them, and burned alive in a house that was set fire to.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can I just hold you there for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: About what time was it on the 10th of June that you located your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: We set out at about 9.00 that morning. We took a bus to Uzice, which was a regular bus line, and we tracked her down at about 11, or between 11 or 12.00 a.m. in a nearby forest. She was there with a couple of her neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And that same day, did you return to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: That's right. We took the same bus back. It was a bus shuttling between Visegrad and Uzice, and at 5.00 that afternoon it drove through that village again on its way back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, how much longer will this procedure take place because this, after all, is Rule 92 ter. If you are going to take a very long time, then we really derive nothing from the procedure which is an abbreviated one.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. There have been delays. I'll try as best I can, Your Honour, to shorten the procedure from here on in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, but could we have the mother's name and the name of that village, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm happy to ask the witness, Your Honour. Could we go into private session for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Counsel has asked for the name of your mother and the village that you --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What else -- what other event helps you establish that it was the 10th of June that you saw these killings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: My sister and I returned to Visegrad. I went to my mother-in-law's flat because my children were there. I found my mother-in-law and asked her to speak to my husband over the phone. He had fled Visegrad and was hiding in Nezuci village. The distance between the two being perhaps a kilometre, a kilometre and a half at the very most. When I came back I spoke to my husband and he asked, Why aren't you running away, why aren't you running from the house? I said, Why should we be? And he said that over in Dusce, at the Varda factory, there was some dreadful things going on, people being killed. He said that in Dusce there was a building or a shed, something to that effect, where people had been burned alive, and he said we should go and take shelter somewhere. During our conversation, my mother-in-law walked up to me and she said to me softly to keep my husband from overhearing this, over the phone, that Milan Lukic was just about parking his car in front of our building. She didn't know Milan Lukic but she was simply assuming that this was Milan Lukic because the car parking outside our house was a dark red Passat.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you go and have a look?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes. I put the receiver down, went over to the window and saw Milan Lukic shut the door on the car and enter our building.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And what subsequently happened in respect of Milan Lukic that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, for interrupting. Just one more clarification, if we could have the number of that house, where was that apartment and number of mother-in-law apartment, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are under a time pressure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, you can ask these questions in cross-examination. I mean counsel will lead the evidence that he wants. If you want to get it, then you ask it in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour. I just try to make shorter my cross-examination and to receive some more information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And, Mr. Cole, you must be coming to an end now. Otherwise, I don't see the point of this as a 92 ter, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you see Milan Lukic this day, close up, after he entered the apartment building of your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: For what period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you about the day that your mother left Visegrad. Did you see your mother the day that she left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: The 14th of June, that's when she left Visegrad. And yes, I did see her that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Where was she when you saw her that day, prior to leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: On the bus on a square in Visegrad that we referred to as the Visegrad Square, which is just next to the old bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Who else did you see in the bus in which you saw your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: All of my mother's neighbours from that village. I saw Milan Lukic on that bus as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What was Milan Lukic doing on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: He was checking people. He asked some women to remove their kerchiefs. He ID'd some, and then at one point, he was midway down the aisle and I heard that he was looking for a young woman, I think the last name was Kurspahic but I don't remember the first name of that woman he was after.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What time did the bus on which your mother departed, what time did it leave Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: On the 14th of June, I can't quite remember the exact time, but they were stuck in that square for a couple of hours. This might have been at about noon, whereas they had arrived that morning at about 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: When was the next day after the 14th of June that you saw your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Five, six days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did she tell you the route that her bus had taken on the 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes, she did. When we saw each other again five or six days later, as I said, she described route that they had taken and it was the same route that I had take on a convoy out of Visegrad on the 17th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What were the towns that your convoy went through leaving Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: It took all sorts of country roads through Simic, Borik. We didn't drive through Rogatica, we just saw it from a nearby hill. We went through Sokolac, we stopped there for as much as an hour, I believe. We drove through Knezine and then we arrived in a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, talking about the 14th of June, the day your mother left on the bus, did you see Milan Lukic again that day after seeing him on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Was he walking in a car, what was he doing when you saw him next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I saw him that afternoon. It might have been around 3 p.m., but I'm not sure of the exact time. It was in the late afternoon, and a large group of people was brought to the square. Some of the women were standing on the steps underneath -- leading up to my building. They said they had all been brought from Zupa when I went down to give them some water. They were all brought there and they were told that they would be put on a convoy and that they would move on. Milan Lukic was in the car, he got out of the car, I saw him walking around the square, around the hotel garden where these people were. I watched all this from the window of my flat, of my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you see these people that were in the square taken somewhere or head off in a particular direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: They were heading them off in a particular direction, yes. I saw them milling around and then there were about 20 soldiers and the men in civilian clothes and the men in various uniforms, and they took them down the main street of Visegrad towards the Mahala neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you remember about what time that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: It might have been, I'm not sure, but it was before it got dark. So it might have been around 5.00 p.m., maybe a little earlier or a little later. I'm not sure of the exact time but there were there in that square a few hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, is not all of this in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I don't think all of this is in the statement, Your Honour. This is one of the incident dates in the indictment of course, the 14th of June, and this is an alibi rebuttal witness who is testifying that she is seen Milan Lukic on this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Because I'm really rethinking now what I said earlier about 92 ter. Of course, if you are proceeding under 92 ter wholly alone and you tender the statement in lieu of examination-in-chief, then that is it. But it may be that once you get out of that mode and you begin to question the witness, that you have moved now into examination-in-chief, and then leading questions would of course not be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I would like to point out that as Mr. Cole references June 4th [sic] as being a reference date in the indictment, in the original statement there was no reference to June 14th whatsoever, much less this issue of the group and the square and seeing Milan Lukic and all of that is new.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us see whether we can conclude this 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I'll move through to the very conclusion of my questions that I've prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, VG-133, I'm going to ask you now to please take a look around the courtroom carefully and tell me whether --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I didn't hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Please wait a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I think we have an objection from one of my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We would object to the form of ID, especially in light of the fact that this is a 92 ter witness and was not noticed as an identification witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we note the objection. And the same for Mr. Cepic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you please take a look around the courtroom carefully, slowly, and tell me whether you can recognize anyone in the courtroom. If you want to stand up to get a better view, please feel free to do so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I don't have to stand up. I can recognize two persons here.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Right. If I could just hold it there. Who is the first person that you can recognize in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: The first person I recognize in the courtroom is Milan Lukic who is smiling at me so nicely now.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, whereabouts is Milan Lukic seated in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Milan Lukic is sitting -- he is the first man sitting right next to the policeman on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Which row?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: The last row. The last row behind the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And what is he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: A suit, a light brown shirt and a dark blue tie with some spots. I can't see the dots very well from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Can the record reflect that the witness has identified the accused Milan Lukic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, have you seen Milan Lukic on television or on the internet at some stage this year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, when you saw him on television or the internet or both, did you immediately recognize it was Milan Lukic or did you have some difficulty recognizing him?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading and relevance given the nature of the identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this trial is very much about identification, and I think out of fairness, it's the sort of question the witness should be allowed to answer. If my learned friend wants to preclude her from saying that, then so be it. In my submission, sir, it's appropriate that she gives the Court guidance on this area of identification by indicating whether she was able to recognize him immediately, had difficulty or whatever else she wants to answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'll allow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So the question was: When you saw Milan Lukic on the television or the internet, did you immediately recognize him as such or did you have some type of difficulty establishing that it was in fact him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I could never have any difficulty in recognizing Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And I'll just ask you this finally: Has the viewing of Milan Lukic on the internet or on television had any effect at all on your identification of him in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Self-serving and leading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not allowing that. I don't think it's beneficial.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, Witness VG-133, who is the other person that you recognized in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you indicate where he is in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: To the left of Milan Lukic and he is wearing glasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Which row is he in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: The last row. Right next to Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And what is he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: I can't see that very well. I'll have to stand up. A suit, a light brown shirt, and a brown striped tie.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could the record reflect that the witness has correctly identified the accused Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you see Sredoje Lukic at some stage this year on the internet or on television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you have any difficulty recognizing --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. As my learned friend raised the same objection about that kind of question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you have any difficulty recognizing Sredoje Lukic on the internet or on television when you saw him this year or did you have some difficulty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-133
utterances.text: No. I've known Sredoje Lukic for over 20 years, and I would never have any problems in recognizing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the very least without waiving any further objections, I would ask for a recess until the a.m. to begin cross. Given the fact that we received this what I'll call as a new statement this morning at 7.53 a.m., we really haven't had a chance to digest it, incorporate it and cross-reference it. Normally the reason we get things early is so we can -- especially when we have them in both languages, is we can discuss statements such as this with the client, prepare, cross-reference, run our own searches, do things of the such, and we have not had a sufficient opportunity to do that with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn now to give Mr. Alarid the benefit of the remaining 12 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, one simple matter in closed session, private session, sorry. It's a very brief matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.
